@Peyman Motlagh Nike is asking for the logic behind Manual Discount Amount in Secure 5. This looks close to Total Discount Modify Amount, the field you defined in https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-21540 as the sum of manual cashier overrides. Can you confirm if it is the same field or a different one, and where it gets calculated.

","created":"2026-09-03T19:52:07.914-0400","updated":"2026-09-03T19:52:07.914-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3327429","author":{"accountId":"5af4956c3eafdb09dee5738a","displayName":"Peyman Motlagh"},"body":"

Hello Damir @damir, 
Although, I cannot share our exact code, I can give you a general idea how we use the PriceOverride records to calculate a Manual Discount Amount for each item:

Manual Discount Amount = system’s original price − cashier‑entered price

If an item never had a manual override, this value is simply 0. If it did, the amount shows how much the manual entry changed the price. The price change is usually a reduction, though it could theoretically be an increase. The related flag, manualpriceflg, is set to 1 whenever a manual price is entered, making it easy to filter for manually priced items.

This is intentionally separate from other discount fields like linediscountamount or trandiscountamount, which come from promotions or coupons applied automatically. Those use different method codes (Promotion or blank) and are not tied to manual overrides.

Here is how the Total Discount Modify Amount is calculated. It is the sum of all manual overrides that occurred in this transaction.

  • Manual Discount Amount is calculated per item.

  • Total Discount Modify Amount is the sum of those item‑level manual discount amounts at the transaction level.

I hope this information is sufficient to answer your questions. 
Thanks

Peyman Motlagh

@damir.demirovic@nike.com
The manualdiscountamount calculation looks only at methodcode = 'PriceOverride' (plus valid before/after prices). It does not look at reason_description at all. So, under the current logic, every PriceOverride event that has a valid previousprice_amount and newprice_amount gets counted into manualdiscountamount identically.  This is regardless of the reason the cashier selected.

That means, using your example: if a cashier keys in a corrected price because the shelf tag was wrong ("Incorrect Price") and a different cashier keys in a reduced price as a goodwill gesture ("Consumer Satisfaction"), both currently produce a non-zero manualdiscountamount for that item, with no differentiation between "this was fixing a data error" versus "this was an actual discount extended to the customer." The field as built doesn't have the concept of manual‑discount = True/False by reason. In this case both case examples you provided will produce manualdiscountamount.

Thanks,
Peyman Motlagh

(Sale_RtlPrcMods / Return_RtlPrcMods / SLfrDlvr_RtlPrcMods)

","created":"2026-09-10T13:54:48.312-0400","updated":"2026-09-10T13:54:48.312-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"5af4956c3eafdb09dee5738a","displayName":"Peyman Motlagh"},"jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3337522","author":{"accountId":"5af4956c3eafdb09dee5738a","displayName":"Peyman Motlagh"},"body":"

Hello Damir, @damir.demirovic@nike.com
Discount Voided Flag only applies to discounts. It does not apply to price overrides. These two things are tracked completely separately in our system: Discounts (promotions, coupons, staff discounts, manual markdowns or anything that would show up under Reason Description) are recorded together in one place, and that's the only place the "voided" flag lives. So if a discount gets voided at the register, that shows up correctly.

Price overrides (anything under Price Override Reason, where a cashier types in a different price by hand) are recorded in a separate part of our data model that was never built with a "voided" flag at all. So today, there isn't a way to tell whether a price override was voided.
Thanks,
Peyman
